published_prior_art.cite: Yata2025Optimal: exact all-rule Gaussian minimax solution under convex centrosymmetry; MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local: selected solutions for two non-nested local regimes.
MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision: establishes multiplicity and qualified exclusions for linear-index rules, not a primitive necessary-and-sufficient classification of the unrestricted correspondence.

MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision excludes only linear thresholds under its stated conditions; Yata2025Optimal gives a centrosymmetric one-index optimum; neither gives the finite curved-score certificate excluding every measurable one-index rule.

Tetenov2012Asymmetric retains threshold structure in point-identified asymmetric settings; no located paper provides the requested rational, globally certified curved least-favorable endpoint-prior witness.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: prop:conditional-tie-uniform-transfer and ass:uniform-two-sided-experiment-equivalence / ass:joint-risk-transfer
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Feasible original-experiment transfer is conditional on uniform two-sided total-variation equivalence, legal bounded estimated games, and joint total-variation approximation; these are not derived from ordinary LAN or from the saddle theorem.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The feasible-regret conclusion is asserted only UNDER those explicitly stated approximation and legality premises, and is secondary to the exact Gaussian-game geometry.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats non-centrosymmetry and directional differentiability in two non-nested cases; Assumption 5 imposes convexity and centrosymmetry for the directionally differentiable case, Theorem 4 supplies a symmetric two-point-prior-supported solution, Theorem 5 is its feasible counterpart, and the conclusion explicitly leaves directional differentiability without centrosymmetry for future work.
The paper gives a finite-sample minimax-regret decision rule among all decision rules under normal errors, with Theorem 1 stated for a convex centrosymmetric parameter space.

Theorem 3 proves infinitely many MMR-optimal rules under stated conditions and rules out linear thresholds under additional differentiability; it does not rule out every arbitrary measurable one-index rule.

source_verification_receipts.version: Econometric Theory First View, published online 23 July 2026
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article studies ex-ante and ex-post robust-Bayes treatment choice using a restricted prior specification, including a symmetric uniform two-point reduced-form prior, rather than Nature ranging over all signed endpoint states in an unrestricted minimax-regret game.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make the rational unbalanced witness the first proof target: provide one explicit finite game/prior candidate before developing the general interval-arithmetic search, so the certificate theorem is tied to a concrete non-index phenomenon.

Turn the indexability OEQ into a generic sufficient theorem on a named open subclass of polyhedral games, with verifiable normal-fan conditions implying a curved least-favorable score; this would move the contribution beyond a single certificate template.
Either instantiate the secondary transfer premise in one named local experiment or remove it from the main narrative and retain it as a clearly separated conditional corollary.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the curved-score certificate and rational-witness OEQ as the focal kernel; treat feasible transfer only as the accepted conditional secondary result.
